skill.name: ai-runtime-memory
skill.description: A local AI runtime memory system for project history, event timelines, and SQL-style memory queries.
skill.summary: Query and maintain local project memory across short-term, long-term, and episodic records.
skill.author: Dwsy

security_audit.summary: Static shell, path traversal, sensitive file, and obfuscation alerts are mostly false positives from Markdown examples, local helper scripts, and dense Chinese documentation. I found no prompt injection, credential access, network exfiltration, or executable obfuscation, but the maintenance documentation includes unsafe file deletion examples that need safeguards.

remediation.issue: Maintenance examples delete short-term memory files without a dry run or confirmation.
remediation.suggestion: Add backup steps, a dry-run command, explicit confirmation, and a narrower file predicate such as -type f before any -delete usage.

remediation.issue: Several examples depend on shell date behavior that differs across platforms.
remediation.suggestion: Document supported shells and provide portable Python alternatives for date-based queries.

semantic_findings.title: Destructive Cleanup Command Lacks Safeguards
semantic_findings.description: Maintenance examples use find with -delete to remove short-term memory files. The commands are limited to local memory paths but should require backup, dry run, and explicit confirmation.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The deletion commands are explicit and target local memory directories. They are documented maintenance steps rather than malware, so the risk is data loss from unsafe execution.

content.user_title: Track Project Memory with SQL-Style Queries
content.value_statement: Project decisions and context can be hard to recover after long sessions. This skill organizes AI runtime memory into local files and provides query tools for timelines, tags, and summaries.
actual_capabilities: Query episodic memory events with WHERE, ORDER BY, LIMIT, and offset options through memory_cli.py.
Format memory query results as table output or JSON output.
Parse YAML front matter and Markdown sections into event metadata.
Run shell helper commands for today, week, recent, search, types, tags, and stats views.
Document a three-layer memory layout with short-term, long-term, and episodic records.
Provide examples for timelines, summaries, backups, validation, and maintenance reports.
limitations: Requires Python 3 and PyYAML for the CLI and parser.
Reads local Markdown memory files; it does not sync to a hosted database.
Some shell examples use GNU date syntax, which may need changes on macOS or Windows.
Stored memory quality depends on accurate event metadata and regular maintenance.

use_cases.title: Recover Project Decisions
use_cases.description: Retrieve past architecture decisions and meeting notes before planning new work.

use_cases.title: Maintain Agent Context
use_cases.description: Keep local AI session memory organized across short-term notes and durable project records.

use_cases.title: Build Timeline Reports
use_cases.description: Create weekly summaries, event timelines, and maintenance reports from structured memory files.

prompt_templates.title: Show Recent Memory
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner check of current project activity.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use ai-runtime-memory to show today's events. Include time, title, type, and tags.

prompt_templates.title: Search By Decision Tag
prompt_templates.scenario: Find a focused set of historical decisions.
prompt_templates.prompt: Find architecture decisions from the last month. Sort newest first and summarize the main outcomes.

prompt_templates.title: Build Timeline Summary
prompt_templates.scenario: Summarize recent work for handoff or review.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review episodic memory for the last week. Create a short timeline with decisions, errors, and follow-up actions.

prompt_templates.title: Assess Memory Health
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect the memory system for stale short-term notes, missing metadata, and tag drift. Recommend safe maintenance steps before any deletion.

output_examples.output: A table-style summary lists each event with timestamp, title, type, and tags. Empty days are reported clearly.

output_examples.input: Find security-related decisions from this month.
output_examples.output: A filtered decision list highlights matching titles, dates, related tags, and a short summary of each outcome.
A maintenance summary identifies stale notes, missing metadata, tag issues, and backup steps to complete first.

best_practices: Review query filters before running shell helpers on important project memory.
Keep event front matter complete so search and timelines stay reliable.
Back up memory files before cleanup or archival tasks.
anti_patterns: Do not store secrets, tokens, or private customer data in memory files.
Do not run deletion examples without a backup and a dry run.
Do not treat remembered context as verified truth without checking source files.

faq.question: What does this skill store?
faq.answer: It stores project memory as local Markdown files with metadata for short-term, long-term, and episodic records.

faq.question: Does it require an external service?
faq.answer: No. The provided tools work against local files and Python scripts in the skill directory.

faq.question: Can it export query results?
faq.answer: Yes. The CLI can print table output or JSON output for further reporting and analysis.

faq.question: Is the shell helper required?
faq.answer: No. It is a convenience wrapper around the Python CLI for common memory queries.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude Code or Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Should I store secrets in memory files?
faq.answer: No. Store only non-sensitive project context, and keep credentials in proper secret management systems.
